mainTopic: Washing out absorbed impure liquid, the dispute about mixtures with blood of exudate, and a new משנה on mixed blood
overview: A ברייתא teaches that a clay vessel that soaked up the urine of a זב or זבה becomes טהור after three rinses with water. If urine was poured in instead of water, it stays טמא even after ten times, because the same kind does not cancel out its own kind. The גמרא says this first opinion is רבי יהודה, who holds מין במינו לא בטיל. It challenges this from רבי יהודה's ruling that water never washes a נדה's spit out of flax. רב פפא answers that spit is different because it is sticky. Next the גמרא asks why the first תנא and רבי אליעזר disagree about fit blood mixed with blood of exudate. רב זביד says the dispute is whether חכמים make a גזירה in the מקדש. רב פפא says everyone makes a גזירה, and the dispute is only whether exudate blood is commonly the larger amount. The wording of the משנה supports רב פפא and leaves רב זביד with a קשיא. A new משנה then rules on other blood mixtures: blood of blemished animals, one unfit cup lost among fit cups, and blood for below the line mixed with blood for above.

steps.title: A clay flask of a זב becomes pure after three rinses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a clay vessel that absorbed the urine of a זב or זבה stays טמא after the first and second rinse, but is טהור after the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a broken clay vessel holding the urine of a זב or זבה is impure the first and second time it is rinsed, and pure the third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a clay vessel that soaked up impure urine and explains how many rinses make it pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urine of a זב or זבה makes things טמא. Clay soaks up liquid, so the urine stays inside the vessel. After three rinses the urine is considered washed out, and the vessel is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay or earthenware vessel, or a broken piece of one
A man or woman with an impure flow, whose urine is a source of טומאה
Ritually impure / ritually pure

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A clay vessel of a זב or a זבה —
phrases.notes: He means a clay vessel that soaked up the urine of a זב or זבה.

phrases.english: the first and second time, it is impure;
phrases.notes: Each 'time' is one rinse of the vessel.

phrases.english: the third time, it is pure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clay vessel that absorbed the urine of a זב or זבה is טהור after the third rinse.

steps.title: Only rinsing with water helps, and urine never does
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule: three rinses help only with water. If urine is put in instead, the vessel stays טמא even after ten times.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was this said? When he put water into it. But if he did not put water into it, it is impure even the tenth time.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains that the three-rinse rule works only when the vessel is rinsed with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is a different kind of liquid from urine, so it pushes the impure urine out. If you keep pouring in urine (even pure urine), the same kind does not cancel out the same kind, so the impure urine is never considered gone.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (limits a rule)
Into it
Tenth

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When he put water into it;
but if he did not put water into it —
phrases.notes: He put urine in instead, the same kind of liquid as what is already absorbed.

phrases.english: even the tenth time, it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the three-rinse rule of step 1 to rinsing with water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three rinses purify only with water; with urine the vessel stays טמא even after ten times.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: three times works even without water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees and says that after the third time the vessel is טהור even if no water was used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: the third time, even though he did not put water into it, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with the limit from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, pouring in urine three times also pushes the impure urine out. He does not accept that the same kind of liquid fails to cancel out its own kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
The third time, even though
he did not put water into it — it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the limit in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After three times the vessel is טהור whether water or urine was used.

steps.title: The first opinion is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the first opinion of the ברייתא as רבי יהודה, because he is the one who holds מין במינו לא בטיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard who says that a kind mixed with its own kind is not nullified? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the first opinion is and answers right away: רבי יהודה. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said urine poured into urine never cancels it out. That is רבי יהודה's known rule, מין במינו לא בטיל. It also means that for רבי יהודה a different kind, like water, does cancel it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard (a way of identifying who holds a view)
A substance mixed with the same kind of substance
Is nullified, cancelled out

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's rule is only about the same kind. He agrees that a different kind, like water, does cancel it out. That is exactly why the next step can challenge him.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says:
a kind with its own kind is not nullified?
Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the author of the first opinion of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the first opinion of the ברייתא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who holds מין במינו לא בטיל.

steps.title: Challenge: for רבי יהודה, water never washes spit out of flax
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that in flax spun by a נדה, רבי יהודה holds that even wetting it with water many times does not remove her spit. That seems to contradict the flask, where water works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted it: flax spun by a נדה, one who moves it is pure. If it was moist, one who moves it is impure because of the liquid of her mouth. רבי יהודה says: even if one wets it with water, it is impure because of the liquid of her mouth, even many times!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that the first opinion of the flask ברייתא is רבי יהודה, using a ruling of his about flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the flask case, water is a different kind and washes out the urine after three rinses. Here רבי יהודה says water does not cancel out the נדה's spit, even after many wettings. So how can the flask ruling be his?

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it (introduces a conflicting source)
Flax
She spun it
One who moves it (impurity through moving, היסט)
The liquid of her mouth, her spit
One who moistens it

phrases.english: And they contradicted it:
Flax that a נדה spun —
phrases.notes: While spinning she wets the thread with her mouth, so her spit is in it.

phrases.english: one who moves it is pure.
But if it was moist —
one who moves it is impure because of the liquid of her mouth.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even one who moistens it with water —
is impure because of the liquid of her mouth,
and even a lot!
phrases.notes: Even after many wettings, the water does not cancel out the spit. That is the opposite of the three rinses of the flask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification of the first opinion as רבי יהודה from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה is the first opinion, who holds that water rinses out absorbed impure liquid after three times.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the flax case רבי יהודה rules that water never cancels out absorbed impure spit, even after many wettings. That contradicts the flask, where three water rinses purify.

steps.title: רב פפא: spit is different because it is sticky
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that spit is different from urine. It is sticky and clings to the flax, so water cannot wash it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: saliva is different, because it is sticky.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule stays the same: a different kind, like water, does cancel out the impure liquid. Spit is a special case because it sticks into the flax and cannot be rinsed out. Urine is thin and washes out of the clay.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Saliva, spit
Thick and sticky, clinging

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, the same kind does not cancel out the same kind, but water does wash out absorbed urine after three rinses. Spit in flax is an exception because it is sticky and clings, so no amount of water removes it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Saliva is different, since it is sticky.
phrases.notes: Literally 'thick': it clings inside the flax, so water can't push it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the nature of spit is different from urine.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The flax ruling seemed to show that רבי יהודה holds water never cancels out absorbed impure liquid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Water does wash out urine. Spit is an exception because it is sticky and clings, so the flask ruling can still be רבי יהודה's.

steps.title: What is the root of the dispute in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a mixture with unfit blood is poured into the drain. Then it asks what principle the first תנא and רבי אליעזר disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if fit blood was mixed with blood of unfit offerings, it is poured into the drain. The גמרא asks: about what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה. It then asks what the real disagreement is between the first תנא and רבי אליעזר. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that fit blood mixed with blood of exudate is also poured out, but רבי אליעזר says it may be used. The גמרא wants the reason behind their argument, not just the two rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of offerings that became unfit
The water channel (drain) in the עזרה, where unusable blood is poured out
"About what do they disagree?" A question asking for the principle behind a dispute

phrases.english: If it was mixed with the blood of unfit offerings,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The same משנה goes on to the case of blood of exudate, where רבי אליעזר disagrees.

phrases.english: it shall be poured into the drain.
About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means the first תנא and רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה after finishing the discussion of רבי יהודה and the flask.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle explains why the first תנא pours the mixture out while רבי אליעזר allows it.

steps.title: רב זביד: they disagree about making a גזירה in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says the dispute is about whether חכמים make a rabbinic גזירה in the מקדש. The first תנא says yes, and רבי אליעזר says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: they disagree about whether we make a גזירה in the מקדש. One Sage holds we do, and one Sage holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives the first answer. The argument is about one general question: do חכמים make protective decrees in the מקדש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא holds that חכמים do make a גזירה in the מקדש. So he forbids this mixture, in case someone comes to use a mixture where most of the blood is bad. רבי אליעזר holds there is no גזירה in the מקדש, so the mixture may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by חכמים to stop people from coming to a real prohibition
"We decree": חכמים make such a protective rule
The בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Zevid says:
They disagree about whether we issue a decree in the Temple.
For one Sage holds: we issue a decree,
and one Sage holds: we do not issue a decree.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר. Some versions say לָא and some say אֵין; both mean "not."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: בְּגוֹזְרִין גְּזֵירָה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether a rabbinic גזירה applies in the מקדש: the first תנא says yes, and רבי אליעזר says no.

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone makes a גזירה; they disagree about how common it is
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says everyone agrees that חכמים make a גזירה in the מקדש. The real dispute is whether it is common for blood of exudate to be more than the blood of the soul.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: everyone agrees we make a גזירה. Here they disagree about whether exudate blood is commonly more than the blood of the soul. One Sage holds it is common, and one Sage holds it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer. In his view, both sides accept the idea of a גזירה. They only argue about whether the worrying situation happens often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר agrees that a mixture with unfit blood must be poured out, because there is a גזירה. He allows only the exudate mixture. The first תנא thinks exudate blood is often more than the blood of the soul, so חכמים made a גזירה on every such mixture. רבי אליעזר thinks that is rare, so no גזירה was made.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, meaning both sides of the dispute
Blood of exudate: the blood that slowly drips out after the main flow of slaughter
Blood of the soul: the blood that gushes out right at slaughter, which is fit for the מזבח
Common, something that happens often

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא says רבי אליעזר rejects a גזירה. In his view, רבי אליעזר agrees there is a גזירה and pours out a mixture with unfit blood. He disagrees only about the exudate case, because he thinks the problem is rare.
steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד: the dispute is whether there is a גזירה in the מקדש at all. רב פפא: everyone makes a גזירה, and the dispute is only whether exudate blood is often the larger amount.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Everyone agrees that we issue a decree;
and here, about blood of exudate
commonly being more than the blood of the soul,
phrases.notes: "More" means a larger amount, so the fit blood would be the minority in the mixture.

phrases.english: they disagree.
One Sage holds: it is common,
and one Sage holds: it is not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גּוֹזְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 7 and rejects רב זביד's idea that the dispute is about the גזירה itself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sides agree there is a גזירה in the מקדש. They disagree only about whether exudate blood is commonly more than the blood of the soul.

steps.title: The משנה's wording fits רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists 'mixed with unfit blood' and 'mixed with blood of exudate' as two separate rulings. That makes sense according to רב פפא, who says רבי אליעזר argues only about the exudate case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רב פפא, this explains why the משנה teaches the cases separately: if it was mixed with unfit blood, pour it into the drain; and if it was mixed with blood of exudate, pour it into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the wording of the משנה as support for רב פפא. This also sets up the challenge against רב זביד that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, everyone agrees that חכמים make a גזירה in the מקדש. So רבי אליעזר agrees that a mixture with unfit blood is poured out, and he argues only about blood of exudate. That is why the משנה keeps the two cases in separate clauses: only the second one has רבי אליעזר's disagreement attached to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this works well according to one opinion (the next line will challenge the other opinion)
That is why the text teaches it this way
Blood of offerings that are unfit
Blood of exudate: the blood that slowly drains out after the main gush of the slaughter

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Pappa,
this is why it teaches:
if it was mixed with the blood of unfit offerings,
it shall be poured into the drain;
(or) with blood of exudate,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, which makes it clearer that these are two separate rulings.

phrases.english: it shall be poured into the drain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two explanations from steps 8 and 9 against the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's explanation that רבי אליעזר argues only about blood of exudate
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists the unfit-blood case and the exudate case as two separate clauses

steps.title: רב זביד cannot explain the separate clauses
steps.stepSummary: According to רב זביד, רבי אליעזר argues about both cases. If so, the משנה should have combined them into one clause. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב זביד, the משנה should have combined the two cases and taught them together! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב זביד from the wording of the משנה and ends with 'קשיא', meaning his view is left with an unanswered problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד says רבי אליעזר holds there is no גזירה in the מקדש, so he would argue in both cases. In that case the משנה should have said 'mixed with unfit blood or with blood of exudate' as one ruling. The separate clauses do not fit his reading, and no answer is given.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the side that has the problem)
Let it combine them and teach them together
A difficulty; the question stands without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: The wording of the משנה supports רב פפא: רבי אליעזר is lenient only about blood of exudate. רב זביד's view is left with an unanswered קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not the same as 'תיובתא'. A קשיא leaves a difficulty unanswered, but it does not fully knock out רב זביד's opinion.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Zevid,
let it combine them and teach them together!
It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other half of the בשלמא structure: what works for רב פפא does not work for רב זביד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר argues about both cases, the משנה would have combined them. Since it keeps them separate, it seems he argues about only one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב זביד's reading stays difficult, and the sugya leans toward רב פפא.

steps.title: Blood of unblemished and blemished animals mixed together
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If blood of unblemished offerings got mixed with blood of blemished animals, the whole mixture is poured into the drain.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If blood of unblemished animals was mixed with blood of blemished animals, it is poured into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a simple ruling about a mixture in one vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of a blemished animal cannot go on the מזבח. Once it is mixed with fit blood, you cannot separate them, so nothing in the mixture is offered and all of it goes into the drain.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; a new משנה starts here
Unblemished animals that are fit to be offered
Animals with a blemish that makes them unfit for the מזבח
The water channel (drain) running through the courtyard of the מקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Blood of unblemished animals mixed with blood of blemished animals:
it shall be poured into the drain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fit blood mixed in one vessel with blemished-animal blood is all poured into the drain.

steps.title: One unfit cup lost among fit cups
steps.stepSummary: A cup of blemished-animal blood got mixed up among cups of fit blood. רבי אליעזר says that once one cup has been offered, all the rest may be offered. חכמים say that even if only one cup is left, it is poured out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a cup got mixed up among other cups, רבי אליעזר says: if one cup was offered, all the cups may be offered. חכמים say: even if all of them were offered except one, that last one is poured into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from blood mixed inside one vessel to a whole cup that is lost among other cups, and it brings an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blood is not blended; one whole cup is unfit, but we don't know which one. רבי אליעזר treats the cup already offered as if it were the unfit one, so the others are allowed. חכמים do not accept this, so as long as a cup is left, it may still be the unfit one and must be poured out.

keyTerms.meaning: One cup mixed up among other cups
Was offered (its blood was placed on the מזבח)
Except for one

phrases.english: A cup mixed up among cups:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
if one cup was offered,
all the cups shall be offered.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ קָרְבוּ כּוּלָּן חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: even if all of them were offered except one of them,
it shall be poured into the drain.
phrases.notes: The one cup that is left is poured out, since it might be the unfit one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה: a whole cup lost among cups, instead of blood blended in one vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: after one cup is offered, the rest may be offered. חכמים: any remaining cup is poured out.

steps.title: Blood for below mixed with blood for above
steps.stepSummary: Blood meant for the lower half of the מזבח got mixed with blood meant for the upper half. רבי אליעזר says to place it above and then again below, treating the lower blood that went above as water. חכמים say all of it is poured out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood that goes below got mixed with blood that goes above, רבי אליעזר says: place it above, and I view the lower blood that went above as if it were water; then go back and place it below. חכמים say: it is poured into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: The third case of the משנה: two kinds of fit blood that need different places on the מזבח get mixed, and רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of blood are fit, but each needs its own place, above or below the line around the מזבח. רבי אליעזר lets the כהן do both placements, because blood put in the wrong place is treated like plain water and does no harm. חכמים do not allow this from the start, so they pour it all out.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that is placed on the lower part of the מזבח
Blood that is placed on the upper part of the מזבח
As though they are water, so they count as nothing
And he goes back and places it again

phrases.english: Blood that is placed below
phrases.notes: Below and above the line that runs around the middle of the מזבח.

phrases.english: that was mixed with blood that is placed above:
Rabbi Eliezer says: he places it above,
and I view the lower ones that were placed above
as though they are water,
and he goes back and places it below.
And the Rabbis say: it shall be poured into the drain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case of the משנה: both bloods are fit, but each needs a different place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: place it above, then again below. חכמים: pour it all into the drain.

steps.title: If he placed it without asking, it is fit
steps.stepSummary: Even according to חכמים, if the כהן did not ask and went ahead and placed the blood, the offering is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did not ask first and went ahead and placed it, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that חכמים' ruling to pour the blood out applies only before the fact. If the כהן already placed it without asking, it is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים pour it out only as the right way to act from the start. Once the כהן has already placed the blood, they do not throw out the offering. In practice their view lines up with רבי אליעזר after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked or consulted (here, asked the rabbis before acting)
Fit, valid

steps.whatToRemember: In the above/below mixture, חכמים say to pour it out at the start, but if the כהן already placed the blood without asking, it is כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between what you should do from the start (pour it out) and what is valid after the fact (the offering is כשר), even according to חכמים.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the כהן placed the mixed blood without asking, the offering is כשר.
